sections.content: How many people are "chief executives and senior officials"?

122,525 people

were counted on the census as "chief executives and senior officials" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Chief executives and senior officials head large enterprises and organisations.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "chief executives and senior officials", 15.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "chief executives and senior officials" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "chief executives and senior officials" included:

  • production managers and directors in manufacturing
  • directors in logistics, warehousing and transport
  • complementary health associate professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "chief executives and senior officials" there were more men than women (72.4% compared with 27.6%).

This means "chief executives and senior officials" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 72.4% and women made up 27.6% of "chief executives and senior officials"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "chief executives and senior officials" included:

  • managers and proprietors in agriculture and horticulture
  • managers in logistics
  • pre-press technicians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "chief executives and senior officials" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "chief executives and senior officials" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "chief executives and senior officials", 6.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (85.8% compared with 14.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (77.8%) than self-employed (22.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Westminster, this is in the same region of London.
